title: Fppf target tests for representable stack morphisms
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $\mathcal Z,\mathcal Y$ algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $f:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$ a morphism representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that its base change by any scheme is an algebraic space. Let $q:W\to\mathcal Y$ be a surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space, with these properties tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Set $Z_W=W\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$, using the 2-fibre product of objects with an isomorphism between their images. Each of the properties affine, finite type, quasi-finite, and separated is preserved by arbitrary base change and satisfies $P(f)\Longleftrightarrow P(Z_W\to W)$, separately for each $P$. A representable stack morphism has $P$ when every scheme base change has $P$. For algebraic spaces, affine means every affine scheme base change has affine scheme source [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; quasi-finite means finite type with finite geometric fibres, where a geometric fibre is base change to the spectrum of an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion, tested by scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text: Fix one of the four properties $P$. The space-level lemma supplies arbitrary base-change stability and fppf descent for this $P$. The representable-pullback-over-space lemma makes $V=W\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ an algebraic space. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, put $A=T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ and $B=T\times_{\mathcal Y}W$. Representability of $f$ makes $A$ a space. To see that $B$ is a space, form the algebraic space $T\times W$ by the space fibre-product lemma, over the common base scheme. The diagonal $\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y$ is representable by the algebraic-stack definition. Its base change to the space $T\times W$ is a space by the representable-pullback-over-space lemma, and is exactly $B$: its objects are a $T$ coordinate and a $W$ coordinate with an isomorphism between their images in $\mathcal Y$. The algebraicity of the stack product used here follows from the algebraic-stack fibre-product lemma. By the scheme-test meaning of the hypotheses on $q$, $B\to T$ is surjective, flat and locally finitely presented, hence is a singleton fppf cover of spaces. No quasi-compactness of $q$ is needed.

Arbitrary stack base change preserves $P(f)$. For $\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$, the 2-fibre product is algebraic by the algebraic-stack fibre-product lemma and the projection is representable: each scheme test of it is, by reassociation, a scheme test of $f$ and hence a space. A scheme test $T\to\mathcal Y'$ of that projection identifies with $T\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z\to T$, which has $P$ by the definition of $P(f)$. For a fixed $T$ coordinate, an object on the iterated fibre product is a $\mathcal Z$ coordinate, a $\mathcal Y'$ coordinate and isomorphisms identifying their images with that fixed coordinate in $\mathcal Y$ and $\mathcal Y'$. Composing these isomorphisms forgets the redundant $\mathcal Y'$ coordinate. Inserting its prescribed image and the identity isomorphism gives an inverse, up to the displayed isomorphisms. These operations also preserve all compatible arrows and the projection to $T$.

Assume $P(f)$. Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to W$, available by the definition of algebraic space. The map $U\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z\to U$ has $P$ by the scheme-test definition of $P(f)$. It is the base change of $V\to W$ along $U\to W$: both 2-fibre products have the same $U$ coordinate, $\mathcal Z$ coordinate and isomorphism of their images in $\mathcal Y$; forgetting the redundant $W$ coordinate gives the comparison and inserting its specified image gives its inverse. The atlas is an fppf cover (etale maps are flat and locally finitely presented, and the atlas is surjective), by the chartwise calculus. Fppf descent of $P$ for spaces now gives $P(V\to W)$.

Conversely assume $P(V\to W)$ and take any scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$. Use $A,B$ from step 1. There is an isomorphism over $B$,
$$A\times_T B\simeq V\times_W B.$$
On objects this is the reassociation of a $T$ object, a $W$ object and a $\mathcal Z$ object with their two isomorphisms to the same image in $\mathcal Y$; composing one isomorphism with the inverse of the other gives the $W$--$\mathcal Z$ comparison. Reversing that composition is the inverse functor, also on compatible arrows. The right side over $B$ has $P$, since it is the algebraic-space base change of $V\to W$. Since $B\to T$ is the fppf cover of step 1, the space-level descent lemma gives $P(A\to T)$. This holds for every scheme test, so $P(f)$. The argument applies separately to each of the four $P$, without assuming any of the other three.

lean.statement: theorem representable_stack_fppf_locality (k : Type u) [Field k] (Z : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (Y : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hZ : IsAlgebraicModuliStack Z) (hY : IsAlgebraicModuliStack Y) (f : BasedFunctor Z Y) (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces f) (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k)))) (hP : P = @MapIsAffine (Spec (.of k)) ∨ P = @MapIsFiniteType (Spec (.of k)) ∨ P = @MapIsQuasiFinite (Spec (.of k)) ∨ P = @MapIsSeparated (Spec (.of k))) (W : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (q : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli W.obj.obj) Y) (hq : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) Y), ∃ (B : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (b : B.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange q T t B b ∧ SpaceMapIsSurjective B T b ∧ ∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ B.obj.obj), IsEtale a → Flat (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ b)).left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ b)).left) : (∀ (Y' : BasedCategory.{v₃, w₃} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (_ : IsAlgebraicModuliStack Y') (g : BasedFunctor Y' Y), IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces (moduliTwoFiberFst g f) ∧ (ModuliAlgebraicSpaceTest P f → ModuliAlgebraicSpaceTest P (moduliTwoFiberFst g f))) ∧ (∃ (V : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (p : V ⟶ W), HasSpaceTargetBaseChange f W q V p ∧ (ModuliAlgebraicSpaceTest P f ↔ P p))
